clue.text: Meat after sandwich perhaps in an Oxford college

indicators.note: after puts the meat behind the sandwich, so it comes second

parts.note: wad is slang for a sandwich or bun, so 'perhaps' marks an example
ham is a meat

explanation.surface: A student buying a ham sandwich in an Oxford college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' sends the meat second. Wad is old British slang for a sandwich or bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Wadham is one of the colleges of the University of Oxford.

clue.text: Rare show designed for stage and screen entertainment

indicators.note: designed says the letters are put together in a new pattern

explanation.surface: An unusual show created for theatre and film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges RARE SHOW.
explanation.definitionFit: War Horse was a hit stage play and a Spielberg film, an entertainment on both.

clue.text: Sort of time to serve up some caramel pudding?

indicators.note: serve up says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Time to bring out some caramel pudding for dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'serve up' reads upwards, reversing the letters found in 'caramel pudding'.
explanation.definitionFit: Duple time is a musical metre with two beats to the bar.

clue.text: Auxiliary note finally omitted from opera

indicators.note: finally omitted from says the note is removed from the end of the opera's name

parts.note: Aida is an opera by Verdi
A is a musical note

explanation.surface: An extra note left out at the end of an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: An auxiliary is a helper, and help or a helper is an aid.

clue.text: Suit: notedly a girl's best friend?

definitions.meaning: one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards
the famous song says these gems are a girl's best friend; 'notedly' means as put to music

explanation.walkthrough: 'Notedly' is a pun: noted as in famous, and noted as in set to musical notes in the Marilyn Monroe song.
explanation.definitionFit: The red card suit and the gemstones of the song share the same name.

clue.text: Modest outlay for South African crossing the Spanish state

indicators.note: crossing says the outlay goes across the other word, holding it inside

parts.note: one rand, I RAND, is a small sum in South African currency
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A South African spending a little to cross over into Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modest outlay' is one rand (I = one), the rand being South Africa's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is a sovereign state, a country.

clue.text: Curse ruling framed by old woman celebrity

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, an old woman

indicators.note: framed by says the ruling sits within the other letters

parts.note: a lion is a celebrity, as in a literary lion
an edict is an official ruling

explanation.surface: A famous woman's mother placing a curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old woman' is mother (MA); 'lion' as celebrity is a dated sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A malediction is a spoken curse, a synonym.

clue.text: English boy upset bellows-mender — blowing this?

indicators.note: upset says the boy word is turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: a boy is a son
Francis Flute is the bellows-mender in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: An English lad, upset, mends bellows while blowing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SON into NOS. The bellows-mender is a character in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose flute is an instrument played by blowing with the nostrils.

clue.text: Excessive rises covered by tabloid in London borough

indicators.note: covered by says the newspaper wraps around the other letters

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: rises says the letters go upwards, read backwards in a down light

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top, excessive

explanation.surface: Excessive price rises reported by a tabloid in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns the excessive word upwards in this down light; 'covered by' wraps the tabloid around it. The Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sutton is one of the boroughs of Greater London.

clue.text: Spymaster in Paris who infiltrates a second resistance movement

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

indicators.note: infiltrates says the French word gets inside the following letters

parts.note: qui is French for who

explanation.surface: A spy chief in Paris sending a person into a resistance group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maquis was the French Resistance in the Second World War.

clue.text: Deny help in retirement, standing around

indicators.note: around says the word for standing wraps the other piece

parts.note: one's standing is one's repute

indicators.note: something in retirement has withdrawn, going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: help means aid

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to help in retirement despite their standing in the community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' looks like old age but means going back; 'around' puts standing outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate a claim is to reject or disown it, a synonym of deny.

clue.text: Last character in register, one who produced noted scores

indicators.note: in says the final letter sits inside the word for register

parts.note: a register is a list
Z is the last character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The last name on a register belongs to someone who scored well.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a composer, so he produced scores written in musical notes.

clue.text: An honest duo, possibly — or a much larger number

indicators.note: possibly says these letters could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A truthful pair, or perhaps many more people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges AN HONEST DUO; the duo suggests two, against which the answer is far larger.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure is a large number compared with a pair of two.

clue.text: Something drunk completely beneficially?

parts.note: a health is a toast drunk to someone
fully means completely

explanation.surface: Something drunk entirely for its good effect.
explanation.walkthrough: To drink someone's health is a toast, so a health is something drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Healthfully means in a wholesome, beneficial way.

clue.text: Hairstyle not initially agreed to? The opposite

indicators.note: not says a letter is taken away from the hairstyle

parts.note: an Afro is a bushy hairstyle

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word agreed

explanation.surface: A hairstyle someone did not agree to at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially agreed' removes A, the first letter of 'agreed', from AFRO. The definition is the phrase 'to and fro'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the pairing to and fro, this word is the counterpart of to, meaning back or away.

clue.text: Communications jargon is making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback says the words are read in the return direction

parts.note: jargon is slang

explanation.surface: Technical jargon in communications coming back into fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a comeback' reverses SLANG IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Signals are messages or communications sent from one party to another.

clue.text: Good to get involved again, producing fruit

parts.note: to re-engage is to get involved again

explanation.surface: It is good to get involved again in producing fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a kind of green plum, a fruit.

clue.text: Maxim of police department backed by corporation

indicators.note: backed says the police department letters go backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
corporation is old slang for a large belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A police department's motto supported by a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns CID into DIC. 'Corporation' is a jokey British word for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictum is a saying or authoritative pronouncement, a synonym of maxim.

clue.text: Lacking caution, he's seen round parts of Leeds

indicators.note: seen round says the first letters go around the others

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: parts of says the city's name is broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A reckless man spotted around parts of the city of Leeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts of' signals the rearranged city name; 'seen round' puts he's around it, the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedless means careless, paying no attention to risk.

clue.text: One travelling to new school in Derbyshire

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative

explanation.surface: A child going off to a new school in Derbyshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Repton is a well-known English public school in the county of Derbyshire.

clue.text: Like assorted ingredients Ed missed in Granny's stew

indicators.note: in puts the shortened word inside the grandmother

parts.note: nan is an informal name for a grandmother

indicators.note: missed says those letters are left out

parts.note: assorted ingredients are varied
Ed is taken as the letters ED

explanation.surface: Granny's stew with mixed ingredients that Ed did not get.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ed' looks like a person but is just the two letters 'missed' from the word for assorted; 'in' then puts the remainder inside the grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: Navarin is a French stew of lamb or mutton with vegetables.

clue.text: Sexless film shown in various quarters

parts.note: an epic is a grand film
E, N and E are compass points, the quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A film without sex scenes being screened in different areas.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarters are points of the compass: East, North, East.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicene means lacking gender characteristics, neither male nor female.

clue.text: Moral code staggering the Irish civil servant at first

indicators.note: staggering suggests the word lurches about, its letters rearranged

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for Irish
CS stands for Civil Service, a civil servant

explanation.surface: A shocking code of conduct for an Irish civil servant at the start of a career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggering' rearranges THE to ETH, which comes 'at first'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethics are the principles of conduct making up a moral code.

clue.text: Staff welcoming old duke's lackey

indicators.note: welcoming says the staff takes the other letters in

parts.note: a staff is a pole

explanation.surface: Household staff greeting an elderly duke's servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A poodle is figuratively a servile follower, a lackey.

clue.text: Private cricket side hosting Worcestershire's opener

indicators.note: hosting says the cricket side holds the other letter inside

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

indicators.note: opener picks the opening letter of the county name

explanation.surface: A private cricket team welcoming Worcestershire's opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is one half of the field; W from Worcestershire, an English county, goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: One's own possessions are private, belonging to oneself alone.

clue.text: Number Domitian initially represented in Rome

parts.note: the first letter of Domitian is D, which as a Roman numeral stands for this figure

explanation.surface: An emperor's image displayed in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Domitian was a Roman emperor; his initial D is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a figure, a cardinal count written as D by the Romans.

clue.text: Turn up with king and queen, received and understood

parts.note: R is short for rex, king

indicators.note: up says the word is read upwards in this down light

parts.note: a turn is a go
ER is short for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Arriving with royalty, being welcomed and appreciated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the turn upwards in this down light, between the king and queen.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio talk, roger is the reply confirming a message has been received and understood.

clue.text: Tool used by medic, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor, a medic
an awl is a pointed tool for piercing

explanation.surface: A doctor's instrument, in a figurative sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a manner of speaking' looks like the idiom 'so to speak' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a slow, lengthened way of talking.

clue.text: Figure getting financial district in right muddle!

indicators.note: in puts the district inside the other letters

parts.note: a muddle is a tangle
EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: Someone in the financial district getting in a muddle over figures.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the City of London's postal district, home of its banks.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle is a geometric figure with four right angles.

clue.text: Karenina's half-hearted collection of reminiscences

indicators.note: half-hearted says half of the name's middle is lost

parts.note: Anna is the first name of Tolstoy's heroine Karenina

explanation.surface: Tolstoy's heroine's unenthusiastic memoirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' drops one of the two middle Ns of ANNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings about a person.

clue.text: Energy in a high degree united all

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy
very means to a high degree
united means made one

explanation.surface: Great energy unites all.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyone means every person, all of them.

clue.text: A bloke's touring arranged by Lewis's neighbour

indicators.note: touring says one word goes round the other

parts.note: a bloke's belongings are his
arr. is the abbreviation for arranged, as in music

explanation.surface: A man's tour organised by his neighbour Lewis.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis and Harris form one island in Scotland's Outer Hebrides, so Lewis looks like a man's name but is a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Harris adjoins Lewis on the same island of the Outer Hebrides.
